sources.title: Introducing LLaMA: A foundational, 65-billion-parameter large language model
sources.evidence: Dated February 24, 2023; announces original LLaMA including 65B, text prediction, and a noncommercial research release with access granted case by case.

sources.title: Original LLaMA model card, llama_v1
sources.evidence: Identifies version 1, FAIR at Meta AI, autoregressive Transformer, 65B variant, bespoke noncommercial license, and research use. Describes a base model without human-feedback training; lists 8192 dimensions, 64 heads and 80 layers for 65B.

sources.title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
sources.evidence: Original paper Table 2 reports 65.2B parameters for the 8192-dimensional, 80-layer, 64-head model. Section 2.2 specifies Transformer, RMSNorm, SwiGLU and rotary embeddings. Reasoning benchmarks evaluate the base model; instruction tuning is discussed separately.

sources.title: Original LLaMA Transformer implementation
sources.evidence: Original-release code at the llama_v1 commit implements causal attention and a dense SwiGLU feed-forward block in each Transformer layer, with no expert router; ModelArgs.max_seq_len is 2048. Token embeddings and output projection are separate modules.

sources.title: Original LLaMA generation interface
sources.evidence: The release generator accepts string prompts and returns decoded strings, truncating combined prompt and generation length to max_seq_len. The exposed interface has generation length, temperature and top-p controls, without a dedicated thinking or tool-call protocol.

sources.title: Original LLaMA release README
sources.evidence: Documents applying for checkpoint access, receiving signed download links after approval, and running the 65B model with eight model-parallel processes.

sources.title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models, Table 1 comparison
sources.evidence: Table 1 explicitly labels the earlier Llama 1 65B model with 2k context and no grouped-query attention. It does not provide a separate active-parameter count for that model.

sources.title: Original LLaMA inference repository code license
sources.evidence: The code repository contains GPL version 3. The model card and announcement separately identify the model as subject to a bespoke noncommercial license; the code license must not be substituted for the model license.

sources.title: Original LLaMA access form
sources.evidence: The historical access form was inaccessible through the web tool. Its complete model license text was not independently retrieved; the supported license classification comes from the announcement and original model card.

name.note: Original first-generation 65B checkpoint; preserve the published variant name despite the more precise rounded paper count.

developer.note: The original card names the FAIR team of Meta AI.

family.note: Normalized catalog family for the original LLaMA release, version 1.

release_date.note: The dated announcement says the models are being released that day. This is the gated research-release announcement date, not evidence that every applicant received weights that day; the arXiv submission followed on February 27.

open_weights.note: Weights were distributed to approved researchers. True means released weights under the catalog convention, not unrestricted public access or an open-source license; present operation of the old access process is not established.

license.note: Descriptive classification supported by original first-party materials. The complete access-agreement text was not retrieved. Do not substitute GPL for inference code or the later Llama 2 community license.

parameters_b.note: Table 2 explicitly reports 65.2 billion for this exact variant. This is the paper-rounded total, not an exact checkpoint tensor count; 65B is the model name. No weights were downloaded.

active_parameters_b.note: Original materials and the later first-party comparison do not separately define an active-parameter total. Dense execution does not justify setting active parameters equal to total parameters.

architecture.note: Dense autoregressive Transformer: the original code applies attention and an unrouted SwiGLU feed-forward module in each of 80 layers; no mixture-of-experts routing.

context_window.note: Original code sets max_seq_len to 2048, and the later paper explicitly reports 2k for Llama 1 65B. This is the combined input/output sequence limit in the released generator, not its shorter example-script default.

modalities.note: The original model performs text continuation; the released generator accepts and returns strings.

reasoning.note: General reasoning benchmark results and chain-of-thought prompting do not establish a dedicated thinking mode. No separately declared thinking capability is provided for this base checkpoint.

tool_call.note: The original release documents text completion and provides no model-native tool-call schema or declared tool-calling support. Leave unknown rather than infer a capability from downstream wrappers.

description.note: The original model card identifies version 1 as a foundational model intended for research.

patch.notes: Gated research weights; open_weights indicates released weights, not unrestricted access or an OSI-approved license. February 24, 2023 is the research-release announcement date; individual download access required approval. The original paper reports 65.2B total parameters, a rounded figure rather than an exact tensor count; 65B remains the variant name. Active parameters and dedicated thinking/tool-call capabilities are not separately documented. The model license is distinct from GPL for inference code.

summary: Reviewed all 14 factual fields against original first-party release materials and the exact Llama 1 comparison row in the later Llama 2 paper. Refine total parameters from the 65B variant label to the original paper's rounded 65.2B figure; confirm dense architecture and 2048-token context. Preserve the gated February 24 research release and noncommercial model-license classification. Active parameters, dedicated thinking and tool-calling remain unspecified. Complete historical access-agreement text and current download access were not verified.
